pitch_detail.notes: The first 60 feet are easy. A clumsy, difficult M6 stretch then gains a stance, and 20 more feet up a stiff dihedral reach the two-bolt belay.

Committing at both the start and the end. Traverse up and right about 12 feet from the belay; the middle is a runout M5 stretch with poor gear where small hatchet-style pins worked well. Finish at a good stance with two bolts.
Climb straight up above the belay on M6 ground with enjoyable hooking above the crux, to a good ledge with no bolts.
Excellent hooking with good footholds. After reaching the big ledge, finish well to the right at the fourth anchor of the Red Route.

review.changed: Four pitches as given. Lead bolts: none placed.

pitch_detail.notes: Shared with the start of Eohippus: corner to a double hand and fist crack, up to a huge ledge.
Traverse northwest to a cleaner corner system, then upward on solid face holds linked by occasional finger and hand cracks, finishing at a small ledge.
Tenuous just off the ground, then a sweet layback crack.
Slopey slab off the ledge, then vegetation to a big red chimney that is better than it looks, though loose blocks sit at the back. Stem up past a chockstone on the right to a good ledge.
Easier wide crack system to a great ledge.
Traverse right to an offwidth, a couple of engaging moves, then keep traversing right on easier ground.

Up and right on stone that looks poor but is solid and very sharp, reaching the summit platform. Since the route traverses west, joining the second and third leads, the fourth and fifth, and the last two on a long rope with plenty of slings keeps the belayer better protected.

review.changed: Seven pitches. No rappel table: descent given loosely (rap off from 10 m east of the summit, then a 40 m rappel to the P6 ledge, then rap the route).

pitch_detail.anchor: 2 stainless bolts at top of ice
pitch_detail.notes: Dependable ice that varies by season; overhanging and hard, M7 or M8 if the ice is not fully formed, with no bolts along it. Some years the chimney gives about 70 feet of hard ice. Protection is scarce through the crux and very traditional.

Hard rock climbing with some loose stone, probably around M6+ (comparable to 5.10 in shoes). The crux is a roof split by a hand crack, with slabby footholds. Two bolts at the end of the technical ground, 30 m higher.

review.changed: Two pitches. No rappel table: one 60 m rope reaches, and the top rappel barely reaches the anchor above the ice.

pitch_detail.notes: Start under the chockstone of the neighbouring route, then about 25 m of steep snow and low-angle ice, followed by about 25 m of excellent steep mixed climbing on good rock and ice.
Mostly easy climbing with a solid mixed crux of about twenty feet.

review.changed: Two pitches; no grades given per pitch.

pitch_detail.notes: Start right of the left-facing dihedral and go straight up the slab, finding gear in the horizontals and some cracks near the arete.
Similar slab climbing between horizontals to a big ledge belay.
Work through overlaps to the right-arching roof, follow it to a #4-size crack at the bulge, pull onto it, traverse right a little and belay at flakes.
Straight up blocky terrain. It can be broken at a nice ledge, or continued.
Free choice of line to the top; the 5.7 flakes are one option.
Unprotectable slab to a grassy platform at the foot of a right-facing corner; usually soloed or walked in from the right.
Up the right-facing corner, pull left, and follow easy ground to a grassy ledge.
Broken terrain into a short finger crack, over the lip and into a ledgy chimney system, where a belay can be set.

The ledgy chimney continues, drifting left. From a grassy ledge, 20 ft of face with nothing to protect it leads to weak gear, then roughly 10 ft more to a reliable finger-size placement. Belay beneath a roof.
Out the left side of the roof onto a ledge, 20 ft of unprotectable face, then flakes to a ledge.
Up and right on flakes toward a big ledge.
Short pitch past corners to a ledge; can link with the previous one if rope drag allows.
Step right and climb solid flakes to a platform at the base of the best pitch.
The standout: 30 m of tight to solid hands, then 15 m of easier topout climbing. Some vegetation in the first 7 ft.

review.changed: Nine pitches. Lower pitches are a choose-your-line affair per the text.

pitch_detail.notes: Start on the ramp to the left or the notch to the right, aim for the left-sweeping crack, undercling and mantle onto the ramp.
Into the recess, under the roof and onto the slab; up toward the clean dihedral, pull an easy roof and belay on ledges to the left.
Straight up toward double fin laybacks, mantle onto a ramp, follow a mossy crack into the offwidth above and belay on a good ledge.

Step right to an undulating hand-size crack to a ledge, then straight up slab with a runout of about 30 ft to a block with cracks taking good gear (a small flake nearby is hollow). Step left round blocks onto low fifth class toward the false summit. Marked PG13.
From the base near boulders at the rubble pile, straight up the slab, placing gear as needed.
Weave through the slab toward the big ledge at the foot of the prominent arch.
Fun pitch: overlapping fins lead to the roof where an arching crack curves rightward. Nice jams and underclings take you to a jagged overlap; surmount it and shuffle along the ledge to a roomy belay.
Flared cracks and slab that ease greatly; pick your own way to the top.
Up the slab, protecting with the dihedral, then past water-eroded features into a gully dihedral that climbs better than it looks if you stay on the good left wall. Belay on a big ledge.
Up and right on easy flakes to the grassy ledge at a minor left-facing dihedral.

Left-facing corner toward the roof; just before it cuts left, place high gear in the weakness on the right and pull the bulge onto the slab. A few slab moves reach ledges that trend right to the base of the large dihedral.
The best pitch: follow the large left-facing corner up and left as it becomes a roof. Lichenous but dry when climbed. Belay at the flake left of the roof.
Up the corner, then move right into a different left-facing corner with awkward moves, aiming for the crack under the bulging roof.
Straight up the corner, pull the roof and belay at flakes above.
Take the left-facing corner to the right trending up and right to a ledge, traverse past an overlap and belay. Going straight up looks good but needs a nut tool as the crack is small and filled.
Traverse right on the ledge to the finger crack that leads to the top.
Meander and traverse by the easiest protectable line to the base of a left-facing corner with a thin crack.
Good corner climbed by laybacking and stemming to a gear belay before the crack turns the right arete. Grade is uncertain and the pitch was wet and slimy when climbed.
The crack wraps around the arete; cross over mostly by hand jams until a pair of cracks reaches a ledge. Much of the traverse is on smears over lichen, and some rock near the belay sounds hollow.
Better to move the belay right and use the fourth pitch of the neighbouring route, Solar Winds, for its finger section; going straight up is a meandering traverse.

review.changed: Four pitches; conditions notes (wet, lichen) kept.

pitch_detail.notes: About 35 m. Stem and jam finger cracks onto a huge boulder, then straight-in jams in single and double cracks (#1-4) to the first bolted anchor.

About 30 m. Hand to wide-hand jams (#2-3) to the Marmot offwidth (#5-6 sizes); two bolts protect the wide section. Then a narrowing splitter, leading to a leftward hand traverse into a second tight hand crack.

pitch_detail.anchor: single bolt, backed up to a cam
pitch_detail.notes: About 15 m. Funky moves into a slot to a no-hands rest; protect thin crack with micro-cams, offsets and RPs in the left-facing corner, then 5.11 moves as the corner flips to right-facing, to a crux bolt. A gear belay with mid-size cams can be built under the right-facing corner if wanted.

About 15 m. Downclimb a little, passing a low bolt, into a layback corner; the first bolt is a leftover exploratory one and should be unclipped after clipping the second. Two more bolts, then a crux mantle to a giant flake and a narrow ledge.

About 30 m. Balance to a potentially dynamic 5.13- reach, which can be bypassed by pulling on a bolt (5.12- A0), but a 5.12- mantle must be done to reach a ledge. Tricky 5.10 past a bolt and chain, then runout slab.

About 45 m. Bottomless chimney just right of the belay; exit on the right, then low-angle corner and slab to an easy hand-jam roof and easier crack. A second with a pack can layback past the chimney if gear was placed right.

review.changed: Six pitches; approximate lengths kept in notes. No rappel table: the text only says each belay has fixed hardware for a single 70 m rope up to P5.

pitch_detail.notes: A right-trending crack and ramp (5.6) is followed by delicate moves leftward onto the snowy ledge top. This pitch is frequently buried in snow.
Traverse left, then climb snow and rock to the main weakness; vertical rock and a chimney to a snowy ledge below the first ice. The belay is a fixed pin anchor, to the right.
A brief ice step to the snow beneath the main pillar, with the belay off to the right. A 70 m rope might allow linking it with the next pitch.

Near-vertical smear to the vertical pillar below the large chockstones, with a fixed pin anchor under the chockstone. Beyond is overhanging ground that was aided on cams and one beak, but could be free in good conditions.
Chimney and gully to the ridge, with several difficult sections. From the ridge, either continue to the summit by the standard east ridge, or rappel the route.

review.changed: Five pitches. No rappel table: only a count of four rappels with two 60 m ropes.

pitch_detail.notes: Set up the belay in the alcove east of the flow base to stay partly out of the avalanche path. Easy 60-degree ice to a short vertical bulge, then a snow ramp to the belay. Becomes buried as winter goes on.

pitch_detail.anchor: tree root with slings, on climber right
pitch_detail.notes: The main pitch, over 70 m. Choose a line up the flow; the right side forms easier but still has sustained vertical stretches. Keep spare screws since the top cannot be seen. Consider an intermediate belay for 60 m ropes, or simul-climb.
Over 60 m of small ice that may fill with snow by midwinter; the anchor sits just short of 60 m.
Over 70 m. Steep snow from the previous anchor, then a 40 ft ice-filled gully, possibly a small roof to stem. Snow above leads to a tree. Rappel anchor on far right of the flow.

review.changed: Four pitches written since the text describes all four; it notes pitches 3 and 4 are rarely climbed.
review.other_findings: Stored 2 pitches; text says guidebooks list four, common ascents are 2-3.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy slab moves, with a left-facing dihedral giving gear at the outset. Zigzag up to the flake marking the start of the hand crack and right-facing dihedral.
Choose the 5.2 hand crack or step right to the 5.6 dihedral; easier than it looks.
Length is roughly 60-70 m; there are many alternate belay spots if a 60 m rope falls short.
Follow the dihedral. Gear is less good than it looks, but small nuts and cams are available.
Free choice. A 5.6/5.7 dihedral on the right is one option, and easier lines run at 5.4-5.5. Walk off south toward Deep Lake on slabby third class.
Scramble the low-angle chimney for about 80 feet, or walk round on the south side, then 40-50 feet of loose third class to a stance below a corner that faces right and leans right.
About 160 feet. Climb the loose corner for 50-75 feet to its end, leave it leftward onto an easy-angled face and keep trending left toward further corners until a reasonable belay appears.
About 160 feet. Reach a clean, left-leaning right-facing corner with a finger crack on its left wall; climb it, then work up and left to a ledge belay.
About 160 feet. Head up corner weaknesses toward the roof with a break, then ramp across the face to cracks beneath it. Belay in a pod.

About 140 feet. Straight up from the pod in a shallow left-facing corner with a thin crack, thin moves up and slightly right, above the roof, then a few more steps rightward reach a second pod. Small cams and wires help.

Several options to the summit; the left line goes under a roof to an old fixed belay then straight up two pitches and joins the north summit descent, while the direct line reaches a notch near the middle summit.

review.other_findings: Stored pitch count 10; text describes 6 entries (7 pitches).

pitch_detail.notes: From a ledge east of the wet chimney, dirty slabs with minimal gear and loose flakes to a small tree with a sling, then easy ramps back toward the chimney. Climb the face east of it until it steepens, then enter the chimney; the crux is passing a big chockstone with smooth walls.

Excellent. Follow cracks starting about 10 feet left of the tree, up a steep right-leaning crack in a corner to a trough, then a chimney system with good stemming. Fixed tat may be present at the belay.

Easy slabs to a yellow nose, undercling and layback the flake left (5.8), corner to the crux overhang with powerful moves to jugs (5.9, felt harder when wet), then dirty slabs to a corner/roof passed on the right (5.7) and ramp to the belay ledge.
Short. Move the belay up and left to a big tree; several dirty routes work. An escape to the southeast ridge exists via the gully east of here.

Runout but easy slabs to a broken corner and chimney with many loose blocks; higher the corner cleans up, a small roof is passed rightward on a layback flake, leading to an easy finger crack. Belay on fourth-class slab.

Long, about 60 m or more, wandering both sides of the arete; simul-climbing or an intermediate belay helps. Loose crest, a detour onto the west face past a fixed pin (5.6), a steep nose (5.7), then easier ground to a boulder on the left of the knife edge.

Delicate traverse across the west face (5.5) to a chimney topped by a fixed pin, with a 5.9 bulge mantle as the crux, then easy ground to the summit. Descend east on fourth class to a tree-limb anchor for a 20 m rappel.

review.changed: Seven entries (pitches 6 and 7 combined as given). No rappel table (one 20 m rappel).

pitch_detail.notes: Leave the big rock to the left, then low-angle terrain trending up and right with sparse protection, many large ledges and a fair amount of turf; may also be ice.
Head up and left with some mixed moves from the belay to an ice runnel, then a big ice panel.
Traverse left across steep snow for 10 m to the main flow, then 50-60 m of 60-70 degree ice.
Pillar feature to a ledge, then the headwall to a rock anchor 40 ft left of the top out.

review.changed: Four pitches; P3 range kept in notes.
